name: Joash
overview: Joash was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the son of Shemaah. He is noted in Scripture for coming to David at Ziklag, indicating his support or allegiance during David's time of refuge. His identification through his father Shemaah provides a specific lineage within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Joash appears once in the biblical record without an associated meaning or divine naming indication. It is presented simply as a proper name without further elaboration in the given text.
familyAndRelationships: Joash is explicitly identified as the son of Shemaah, establishing a direct familial relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family connections for him in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Joash's significance lies in his association with David during a critical period at Ziklag, suggesting his allegiance to the future king of Israel. His presence among those who joined David highlights the gathering of support from the tribe of Benjamin. This connection to Shemaah and his coming to David exemplify the consolidation of loyal followers around God's anointed leader.
